subject: Software Factory Design Patterns: Build vs. Buy Your Agentic Stack
body:
Hello First Name,

This week's 🦄 ai that works session was on "Software Factory Design Patterns: Build vs. Buy Your Agentic Stack"!

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot on the architecture of the enterprise software factory, its four core layers, and the buy vs. build decisions at each one. Here's a quick rundown:

*   **The Agentic Software Factory has Four Core Layers**: Compute, Dev Environment, Harness (inner/outer), and Orchestration (control plane).
*   **Critical 'Buy vs. Build' Decisions at Each Layer**: We talked about choices ranging from managing your own MacBooks for compute to using vendor harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex) or building custom orchestration. It's not just about big vendors; every decision impacts flexibility and control.
*   **The Dev Environment Layer is Especially Tricky**: We explored 'pets vs. cattle' setups and the complexities of multi-repo, multi-service applications for agents. A key takeaway is how crucial well-defined interfaces are between these layers for flexibility and scalability.

The main takeaway from this session is this: Building an agentic software factory isn't about buying a monolithic solution or building everything from scratch. Instead, it's about deeply understanding those four core layers and leveraging open interfaces to compose the best tools for your specific needs.

We also had a fascinating session last week about "Designing Agentic Workflows." We explored how to structure complex multi-agent systems, and you can find the video, whiteboards, and code on GitHub!

Our next session tomorrow will be all about "Optimizing LLM Costs and Performance," where we'll explore practical strategies for efficient agent deployment.
Sign up here: https://lu.ma/zcf5c8yd

If you have any questions, just reply to this email or ask on Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We're always happy to help! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
call_to_action: Review the session recording and code on GitHub, and sign up for our next session on LLM costs and performance.
